title: The Peutinger Table: a Roman road map that squashed the world
excerpt: I set a Roman road map 6.75 m long beside a modern one. It squashes the world 11 times north to south, yet 53% of its road distances are within 25% of the real road, and it switches to Gallic leagues exactly where it says it does.
seo_description: The Peutinger Table beside a modern map: 465 places, 1,558 road legs measured, a world squashed 11 times, and where Rome falls.
header_alt: Title card reading 'Peutinger Table' in black and red on pale parchment, above a thin strip of Miller's facsimile of the whole Roman road map dotted with coloured markers, a small modern map of Europe, North Africa and the Middle East with the same places, and the figures '11x squashed north to south' and '53% of legs within 25% of the road'.
